text:
cheng: heads-up: noticed a small p99 regression in host ingress after the preparse-lite change in canary (deploy r-2026-03-21-8)

sara: saw it too, p50 steady but p99 +12ms on long tails. stack traces point at parse/emit path, smallwrite bursts over grpc.

jamal: uploaded profiler snapshot -> https://console.redwood.ai/perf/snapshots/1716504321 : flame shows ~30% more time in `proto_unmarshal` and ~18% extra syscall time from `writev` for tiny frames

nina: guess: fragmentation increased so KV cache hit locality is worse (more mini-requests), causes more context switches. canary traces show more KV lookups per request

cheng: exact numbers: baseline p99 128ms -> canary 140ms. avg tokenization unchanged. KV cache miss rate up from 2.1% -> 7.4% for that shard during spike window

carter: interesting — kernel selection may be forcing smaller vectorized paths due to shorter sequence length after preparse. if runtime picks scalar kernels more often, that'll explain CPU jump

sara: jamal can you paste the kernel fingerprint logs? I see `kernel_choice=auto, backend=avx2, path=scalar` for a lot of samples

jamal: here: ```[1716504300] fingerprints: seq_len=8 -> scalar, seq_len=64 -> vectorized; auto-threshold at 32``` also saw more `grpc_writev` syscalls

nina: quick mitigation suggestion: temporarily disable preparse reordering for requests under 128 bytes or force coalescing at ingress to reduce writev fragmentation

cheng: can we try two experiments in parallel on a small canary group:
- ingress: enable coalesce_small_writes=true
- runtime: bump kernel auto-threshold from 32 -> 24 to prefer vectorized path earlier

carter: also suggest hunting batching heuristic: current minibatch max-delay 2ms might amplify small bursts. try 4ms for canary

jamal: i can spin a canary with those three flags. also will re-run perf snapshot and kv telemetry. planning deploy in 15m :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy request created: canary/ingress-coalesce+kernalthresh+batch-delay - id canary-1716504350

ci-bot: canary smoke pass failed on 2/10 instances (timeout at 5s) - logs: ```grpc: timeout waiting for writev ack``` investigating

sara: hmm timeouts correlate with instances that had highest KV miss spikes. maybe coalesce caused batching that overloaded small KV shard

nina: if coalesce overloads shard we can instead try ingress-rate-limit small-reqs to spread across shards (cheap temporary fix)

cheng: agree. jamal, hold the canary scale-up. instead test kernel-threshold + batch-delay only, then we can iterate on coalesce after KV guardrails

jamal: acknowledged. rolling back coalesce flag, keeping kernel-thresh=24 and batch-delay=4ms on 3 canary hosts. snapshot scheduled

jamal: new snapshot: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/snapshots/1716504470 — p99 back down to 130ms but not fully baseline. kernel-path vectorized samples increased by 12%

carter: that matches hypothesis. next: long term we should add a smallwrite-coalescer in the host proxy that does adaptive coalescing based on KV load and writev queue length

sara: created an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/1457 - title "adaptive small-write coalescer + KV-aware ingress". assigned to @carter and @nina

cheng: good thread. next steps: 1) finish perf snapshots 2) telemetry alert for KV miss rate >5% on shard 3) design ingress coalescer with throttles

nina: will draft design doc and mock telemetry dashboards by EOD :memo:

carter: i'll prototype the coalescer shim and a heuristic that watches `kvcache.hit_rate` and `writev.queue_len`

sara: thanks all. keep pings in this thread with new snapshots or if any other canary blips show up :eyes:
